formats.key: depositInstant(address tokenIn, uint256 amountToken, uint256 minReceiveAmount, bytes32 referrerId, address recipient)
effects: The signer pays amountToken (18-decimal units) of tokenIn. The amount less the fee goes to tokensReceiver and the fee goes to feeReceiver, both set in storage.
The vault mints mintAmount of the vault's mToken (set in storage) to recipient. The call reverts if mintAmount < minReceiveAmount.
The mint amount is net of the fee and uses the oracle rates of tokenIn and the mToken.
totalMinted[signer] goes up and the token's vault allowance goes down. This is bookkeeping only.
formats.shown: "instantly buy", then the payment token by name, the amount as a bare number, a minimum to receive as a bare number with no token, and the receiver address.

findings.title: depositInstant shows 'Minimum to Receive' as a bare number and never names the mToken received
findings.evidence: DepositVault._depositInstant: `mToken.mint(recipient, result.mintAmount);` with mToken from storage. Descriptor field 'Minimum to Receive' uses format unit, params {"base":" ","decimals":18}. Case 0 shows "0.001 " while mAPOLLO arrives. The blind reader wrote "unnamed Midas token".
findings.fix: Split the descriptor per vault and add a token constant for each mToken, then use tokenAmount with that token. Or at least name the token in the label or intent, e.g. "Buy mToken instantly".

findings.title: depositInstant shows the paid amount with a blank unit, apart from its token
findings.evidence: Descriptor field 'Amount' uses unit with base " " and decimals 18 (amountToken is in base 18, per `_tokenTransferFromUser` convertFromBase18). Case 0 shows "2 " next to 'You pay with: USD Coin'.
findings.fix: Label the field 'Amount to pay (in token units)', or put the token and amount together in an interpolatedIntent such as "Buy with {amountToken} {tokenIn}".

findings.title: depositInstant intent 'instantly buy' does not say what is bought or what is paid
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent: "instantly buy". There is no interpolatedIntent. The function mints the vault's mToken in exchange for tokenIn.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Buy mToken with stablecoin" and add an interpolatedIntent that names the amount, tokenIn and recipient.

cases.notes: 2 USDC out is shown right. mAPOLLO arrives (1.867), but the screen gives only a bare minimum of 0.001 and no token name.

formats.key: depositInstant(address tokenIn, uint256 amountToken, uint256 minReceiveAmount, bytes32 referrerId)
effects: The signer pays amountToken (18-decimal units) of tokenIn. The amount less the fee goes to tokensReceiver and the fee goes to feeReceiver.
The vault mints at least minReceiveAmount of its mToken to the signer (msg.sender). Otherwise the call reverts.
The mint amount is net of the fee and uses the oracle rates.
formats.shown: "instantly buy", the payment token by name, the amount as a bare number, and a minimum to receive with no token name.

findings.title: depositInstant (no recipient) shows the minimum received without naming the mToken
findings.evidence: DepositVault.depositInstant passes msg.sender to _depositInstant, which runs `mToken.mint(recipient, result.mintAmount)`. Field 'Minimum to Receive' is unit with base " ". Case 1 shows "0.9476672238 " and mTBILL arrives. The blind reader: "which token is not shown".
findings.fix: Add a token constant for each vault's mToken (one descriptor per vault) and use tokenAmount, or name the mToken in the label or intent.

findings.title: depositInstant shows the paid amount with a blank unit, apart from the payment token
findings.evidence: Field 'Amount' is unit, base " ", decimals 18. Case 1 renders "1 ".
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent "Buy with {amountToken} {tokenIn}", or relabel the field to tie it to the token.

findings.title: depositInstant intent 'instantly buy' does not name the asset bought or paid
findings.evidence: Descriptor intent: "instantly buy". There is no interpolatedIntent.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Buy mToken with stablecoin".

cases.notes: 1 USDC out is shown right. 0.9478 mTBILL arrives, but the screen shows a minimum of 0.9477 with no token name.

formats.key: depositRequest(address tokenIn, uint256 amountToken, bytes32 referrerId)
effects: The signer pays amountToken (18-decimal units) of tokenIn now. The amount less the fee goes to tokensReceiver and the fee goes to feeReceiver.
A pending mint request is created for the signer. Nothing is minted in this call.
Later, an admin can approve the request and mint mToken at a rate the admin picks (newOutRate), or reject it. On rejection the code sends no refund.
There is no minimum on the mToken the signer gets later.
formats.shown: "Deposit Request", the payment token by name and the amount as a bare number.

findings.title: depositRequest intent does not say the payment leaves now and the mToken mint waits on an admin
findings.evidence: DepositVault._depositRequest calls `_tokenTransferFromUser(tokenIn, tokensReceiver, ...)` at once and stores `status: RequestStatus.Pending`. Minting happens only in the admin-only `_approveRequest`. `rejectRequest` sets status to Canceled and returns no tokens. The descriptor intent is "Deposit Request".
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Pay now, mToken minted after approval" and add an interpolatedIntent with the amount and tokenIn.

findings.title: depositRequest has no bound on the mToken received; an admin sets the rate at approval
findings.evidence: DepositVault._approveRequest: `uint256 amountMToken = (request.usdAmountWithoutFees * (10**18)) / newOutRate;`, where newOutRate is an onlyVaultAdmin input.

findings.title: depositRequest shows the paid amount with a blank unit, apart from the payment token
findings.evidence: Field 'Amount' is unit, base " ", decimals 18. Case 2 renders "100 " next to 'You pay with: Tether USD'.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent "Pay {amountToken} {tokenIn} for a mint request".

findings.title: depositRequest's only test case is a reverted transaction, so no effect is checked on chain
findings.fix: Add a test from a successful depositRequest transaction.

cases.notes: The mined transaction reverted, so there are no signer effects. Judged from the code only.

formats.key: depositRequest(address tokenIn, uint256 amountToken, bytes32 referrerId, address recipient)
effects: The signer pays amountToken (18-decimal units) of tokenIn now. The amount less the fee goes to tokensReceiver and the fee goes to feeReceiver.
A pending mint request is created with recipient as its beneficiary. On admin approval, recipient gets the mToken, not the signer.
An admin sets the mint rate at approval or rejects the request. There is no refund in code and no minimum.
formats.shown: "Deposit Request", the payment token by name, the amount as a bare number and the receiver address.

findings.title: depositRequest (recipient) intent hides that the payment is immediate and the recipient's mint depends on an admin
findings.evidence: DepositVault._depositRequest: `mintRequests[requestId] = Request({sender: recipient, ... status: RequestStatus.Pending ...})` after `_tokenTransferFromUser(tokenIn, tokensReceiver, ...)`. The intent is "Deposit Request".
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Pay now, mToken minted to receiver later" and add an interpolatedIntent with amount, tokenIn and recipient.

findings.title: depositRequest (recipient) has no bound on the mToken the recipient gets later
findings.evidence: DepositVault._approveRequest: `amountMToken = (request.usdAmountWithoutFees * (10**18)) / newOutRate;`, where newOutRate is an admin input.

findings.title: depositRequest (recipient) shows the paid amount with a blank unit
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent that puts {amountToken} next to {tokenIn}.
